items.impact: The concept inventory visibly proposes plugin installation/local addition alongside reload, MCP, and skill-management controls, preserving useful GUI source lineage for later owner adjudication.
items.statement: This window inventories plugin, MCP, and skill-management settings, including numeric and checkbox inputs, add/reload actions, an MCP provider selector, and a password input, but does not promote them to production behavior.
items.title: Plugin, MCP, and skill settings are preserved as concept controls

items.impact: Promotion without an owner-defined secret boundary could expose credentials or create a nonfunctional security-sensitive field with no persistence, redaction, revocation, error, or acceptance semantics.
items.statement: The MCP password control has no canonical command, wiring key, storage authority, lifetime, redaction, validation, failure recovery, or receipt contract; those choices cannot safely be delegated to a builder.
items.title: MCP credential handling is intentionally uncontracted

evidence.exact_quote: "owner_rationale": "Owner-adjudicated as concept/source-lineage only. This control is not production evidence and is not promoted until a canonical owner doc accepts the behavior and a production wiring row supplies command/state/receipt/test evidence."

items.impact: The reconciliation record prevents concept controls from being mistaken for build-ready requirements and names the evidence classes required before promotion.
items.statement: The repeated owner rationale is an explicit governance boundary: canonical owner acceptance plus command, state, receipt, and test evidence is required before any control in this segment becomes production truth.
items.title: Concept lineage is explicitly barred from production evidence

items.impact: The concept captures discoverable global and per-server LSP toggles for rust-analyzer, tsserver, pyright, and lua-ls, plus registry search and custom-server entry points.
items.statement: The LSP registry concept includes search filtering, a global enable switch, individual server enable switches, and a custom-server action; current handlers only express toast-level visual behavior.
items.title: LSP registry and enablement controls are inventoried

items.impact: A promoted GUI could report enabled or opened states without starting, stopping, configuring, health-checking, or recovering a language server, producing misleading state and untestable failures.
items.statement: No canonical command, persisted state model, process ownership, startup/timeout/retry behavior, partial-failure recovery, network-loss behavior, observability receipt, or acceptance oracle is supplied for global, per-server, or custom LSP operations.
items.title: LSP controls can toast success without an executable lifecycle

items.impact: The inventory preserves proposed shortcut scope, key capture, reset/export/import entry points, and configurable chat-command tokens for later ownership decisions.
items.statement: This segment proposes scoped shortcut binding and editable chat-command aliases, including /settings, /model, and /effort, while remaining concept-only.
items.title: Shortcut and chat-command configuration is represented

items.impact: Unspecified reset and import semantics could erase bindings, accept malicious or incompatible files, or leave a partially applied keymap with no deterministic recovery path.
items.statement: Reset-all and export/import lack confirmation scope, format/version validation, conflict policy, atomicity, rollback, backup, permission, and falsifiable success/failure receipts.
items.title: Shortcut reset and import have no safety transaction

items.impact: Builders and users cannot determine units, valid limits, localization, performance effects, or how invalid values should be announced and recovered.
items.statement: The LSP Timing & Behavior number inputs expose bare numeric labels such as 300, 2000, and 1000 without semantic names, units, minimums, maximums, overflow behavior, or validation oracles.
items.title: LSP timing numbers are unlabeled and unbounded

items.impact: If promoted as editable aliases without an immutable authorization boundary, approval or evidence revocation could be ambiguous, spoofable, accidentally invoked, or dispatched under the wrong principal or scope.
items.statement: The proposed /revoke-evidence and /approve text controls have no canonical command IDs, parser rules, collision handling, caller identity, authorization scope, confirmation, audit receipt, replay protection, or failure behavior.
items.title: Privileged chat aliases have no authority boundary

items.impact: Without an owner-defined precedence and propagation model, application and project rule sources may conflict, load stale content, or apply to an unintended project or agent.
items.statement: Application and project rule paths are named, but their authority, path trust boundary, precedence, merge behavior, reload trigger, invalid-file handling, propagation consumers, and observable applied-version receipt are unspecified.
items.title: Rule source precedence and propagation are undefined

evidence.exact_quote: "owner_rationale": "Owner-adjudicated as concept/source-lineage only. This control is not production evidence and is not promoted until a canonical owner doc accepts the behavior and a production wiring row supplies command/state/receipt/test evidence."

items.impact: The explicit owner boundary keeps rule, command, and editor concepts from silently becoming implementation discretion.
items.statement: The segment consistently declares that owner acceptance and production wiring evidence are prerequisites for promotion.
items.title: Owner adjudication remains a hard promotion gate

items.impact: Concurrent, interrupted, cross-filesystem, or conflicting copy/move operations could overwrite data, duplicate files, strand partial output, or present success before durability without a specified recovery route.
items.statement: The file-manager conflict and copy/move controls do not define source/destination validation, overwrite confirmation, keep-both naming, symlink and traversal policy, atomicity, cancellation, concurrency, partial-failure cleanup, undo/rollback, or durable receipts.
items.title: File overwrite and move semantics lack data-loss safeguards

items.impact: The likely port setting cannot be safely validated or localized from the inventory alone, and malformed or privileged port values have no defined error behavior.
items.statement: The SSH & Debug section exposes a number input labeled only 22, with no semantic field name, allowed range, defaulting rule, privilege constraint, or validation oracle.
items.title: SSH port intent is only implied by a bare value

items.impact: Promotion without an explicit trust and credential model could leak passwords or keys, silently fall back to weaker authentication, or leave users unable to diagnose host-key, agent, or network failures.
items.statement: The SSH key/password/agent selector lacks credential-source authority, secret storage and clearing, host-key verification, fallback ordering, prompting, offline behavior, failure recovery, and audit/diagnostic receipt semantics.
items.title: SSH authentication choices lack a trust boundary

items.impact: The concept at least records selected-state and tablist semantics for Terminal, Problems, Output, Ports, Browser, and Debug, providing an accessibility-oriented shape for later owner work.
items.statement: The bottom panel models a tablist with Terminal initially active and uses aria-selected and roving tabindex values to represent the visible tab state.
items.title: Bottom-panel tab state has partial semantic modeling

items.impact: Keyboard and assistive-technology users may be unable to change tabs even though the controls advertise tab roles and selectable state.
items.statement: Every visible bottom-panel tab is click-driven and explicitly flagged as lacking keyboard parity; no Arrow, Home, End, Enter, or Space transition contract is supplied.
items.title: Bottom-panel tabs advertise semantics but exclude keyboard operation

evidence.exact_quote: "Contains mock/demo/local fixture state and is excluded from acceptance evidence unless replaced by a real state contract."

items.impact: The mock terminal, problem, browser-session, and local-host data cannot be used to claim implementation or acceptance closure.
items.statement: The reconciliation record explicitly classifies the bottom-panel data and actions as concept fixtures and excludes them from acceptance evidence until backed by a real state contract.
items.title: Fixture-only bottom-panel state is explicitly non-evidence

items.impact: A production-looking Reveal in Terminal or Focus shell action could be mistaken for a wired capability despite having only demo dispatch, no canonical command, no authoritative state transition, and no receipt or test oracle.
items.statement: The terminal buttons carry command-like tokens and call PM_TERMINAL_DEMO, but canonical_command_id and wiring_matrix_key remain null and the controls are fixture-only.
items.title: Terminal command tokens are not production command evidence

items.impact: Users who cannot use a pointer may be unable to reveal diagnostic sessions or switch Console, Network, and Evidence content, while assistive technology receives no reliable interactive semantics.
items.statement: Problem rows and Browser subtabs use onclick handlers on non-interactive tr and span elements and are explicitly flagged for missing roles and keyboard parity.
items.title: Diagnostic rows and Browser subtabs are pointer-only

items.impact: A disabled bottom-panel control can appear broken or permanently unavailable without telling the user which prerequisite, failure, permission, or recovery action applies.
items.statement: The disabled checkbox state has no visible reason reference or specified linkage to a prerequisite, diagnostic explanation, or recovery action.
items.title: Disabled bottom-panel state has no explanation

evidence.exact_quote: "Contains mock/demo/local fixture state and is excluded from acceptance evidence unless replaced by a real state contract."

items.impact: The show-problems demo cannot be counted as production wiring or acceptance proof merely because it contains a plausible command token.
items.statement: Show Problems is explicitly bound to PM_TERMINAL_DEMO and classified as concept_fixture_only, with fixture state excluded from acceptance evidence.
items.title: Show Problems remains explicitly fixture-only

items.impact: Users cannot distinguish an intentional prerequisite gate from a defect, permission denial, unsupported capability, or recoverable runtime failure.
items.statement: Two disabled bottom-panel checkbox controls are explicitly flagged as missing a visible reason reference and have no command, state owner, or recovery explanation.
items.title: Disabled controls conceal prerequisites and recovery

items.impact: Binding, creation, or unbinding could target the wrong worktree, lose association with dirty work, race filesystem or Git state, or become inaccessible to keyboard users, with no defined rollback or receipt.
items.statement: Worktree selection, creation, and unbinding are click handlers on concept-only controls with no canonical commands, authorization scope, dirty-state interlock, concurrent-change check, atomic transition, rollback, durable receipt, or keyboard-operable role and name contract.
items.title: Worktree binding actions lack authority, safety, and keyboard semantics

evidence.exact_quote: "label": "42k/128k Usage 42,180 / 128,000 Input 38.2k tokens Output 3.9k tokens Compact Now More Details",

items.impact: Static token counts and a production-looking Compact Now affordance can misrepresent current capacity or trigger an irreversible context transformation without explaining freshness, scope, eligibility, progress, failure, or resulting evidence retention.
items.statement: The usage hover control embeds fixed usage values and Compact Now text in a click-only span with no role or keyboard parity, canonical command, live-data source, staleness model, compaction transition, failure recovery, or acceptance receipt.
items.title: Usage and compaction UI can present stale or unsafe state

segments.summary: Reviewed all plugin, MCP, and skills concept controls; retained the explicit promotion boundary and identified the unowned credential lifecycle and execution contract.
Reviewed formatter and LSP registry controls; the proposed search and toggle surface is preserved, while toast-only handlers lack a production lifecycle, recovery, and oracle contract.
Reviewed LSP timing, shortcut, and chat-command settings; reset/import safety and numeric input semantics remain uncontracted.
Reviewed privileged chat aliases, rule-source fields, and editor UX concepts; approval/revocation authority and rule precedence are unresolved, while owner adjudication remains explicit.
Reviewed editor and file-manager settings through the start of SSH & Debug; file mutation safety and the implied SSH numeric field remain undefined.
Reviewed SSH authentication settings and bottom-panel tabs; partial tab semantics exist, but credential trust and complete keyboard operation are absent.

Reviewed bottom-panel collapse, terminal, Problems, Ports, Browser, and subtab controls; fixture exclusion is clear, while production binding, keyboard semantics, and disabled-state explanations are missing.

Reviewed show-problems, disabled states, worktree binding/create/unbind, and usage/compaction controls; fixture boundaries are explicit, but destructive authority, transaction recovery, live-state truth, and accessibility contracts are absent.

cross_document_questions: Which canonical owner document accepts or retires each plugin, MCP, skill, formatter, LSP, shortcut, rule, editor, file-manager, SSH, bottom-panel, worktree, and usage control family?
Where are the production command, authoritative state, handler, receipt, and test rows for any concept control that is promoted?
Which canonical security owner defines MCP secret lifecycle, SSH authentication trust, privileged approval and evidence-revocation authority, and worktree mutation authorization?
Which canonical GUI owner defines keyboard interaction, visible disabled reasons, stale-data presentation, and error or recovery states for the bottom-panel and usage surfaces?

Atomic copy move overwrite keep-both conflict recovery and cancellation UX contracts
Accessible tablist and custom interactive-row keyboard behavior for desktop GUI frameworks

Live token usage freshness and user-visible context compaction progress failure and recovery patterns
